tools.name: remove_platform_scaffold
tools.description: At the exact current revision and confirm=true, remove only editor-owned generated Android, iOS, or Dedicated Server scaffold files and restore package scripts replaced by generation; preserved game-owned server hooks are not deleted.

tools.name: validate_ios_generated_project
tools.description: Validate one exact experimental Swift iOS scaffold revision, all editor-owned hashes, Xcode project/scheme structure, SwiftUI entry point, WKWebView host, and Info.plist markers without compiling, signing, or launching it.

tools.name: validate_platform_build_matrix
tools.description: Validate every authored Build Profile together with its current host/toolchain/scaffold readiness and report separate project-export and native-package readiness without building, installing, signing, or deploying.

tools.name: get_installed_platform_restart_status
tools.description: Inspect exact Build Profile revision, host/toolchain/scaffold readiness, deterministic diagnostic fingerprint, and latest relaunch evidence for one platform without saving or restarting the editor.

tools.name: plan_installed_platform_restart
tools.description: Create a bounded, single-use five-minute restart lease for installed project platform support under one exact diagnostic fingerprint; this does not save or relaunch the editor.

tools.name: restart_editor_for_installed_platform
tools.description: Consume one exact, non-expired platform restart lease, persist the project, and schedule a Zvibe Editor relaunch that reopens the same project with verifiable target/plan evidence.

tools.name: get_device_tooling_capabilities
tools.description: Read the honest Device Simulator and remote Device Lab support inventory, including simulated Application/Screen/SystemInfo classes, transport/security model, supported player commands, platforms, and explicit non-simulated limitations.

tools.name: list_device_simulator_profiles
tools.description: List immutable built-in and project-owned custom Device Simulator definitions, the exact custom-catalog revision, and the active profile id.

tools.name: set_device_simulator_profile
tools.description: Create or exactly replace a project-owned custom device definition. Built-in definitions are immutable; pass every device field and the exact catalog revision returned by list_device_simulator_profiles.

tools.name: delete_device_simulator_profile
tools.description: Delete a project-owned custom profile under the exact catalog revision. Active references are cleared; immutable built-ins cannot be deleted.

tools.name: activate_device_simulator_profile
tools.description: Apply a built-in or custom definition to the actual preview engine view under the current simulation revision, optionally choosing orientation and enabled state. Returns normalized simulated Application, Screen, and SystemInfo values.

tools.name: start_device_lab
tools.description: Start a bounded version-1 WebSocket Device Lab and mint a non-persisted, expiring pairing token. Defaults to loopback and an automatic port; LAN listening requires confirm=true and should only be used on a trusted network because transport TLS is external.

tools.name: stop_device_lab
tools.description: Stop the listener, reject pending commands, discard the ephemeral pairing token, and disconnect all remote players.

tools.name: get_device_lab_status
tools.description: Read listener state, address, pairing expiry/availability, connection and pending-command counts, errors, and security posture without revealing the live token.

tools.name: list_remote_devices
tools.description: List authenticated remote-player identities, advertised capabilities, connection activity, and bounded evidence counts.

tools.name: get_remote_device_logs
tools.description: Read a bounded, paginated copy of one connected player's structured console stream with optional level and text filtering.

tools.name: get_remote_device_metrics
tools.description: Read bounded, paginated remote FPS/frame-time/draw-call/resource samples and numeric min/max/average summaries.

tools.name: capture_remote_device_screenshot
tools.description: Request and return a bounded PNG screenshot from a connected player that advertised screenshot support.

tools.name: send_remote_device_input
tools.description: Send one confirmed normalized primary-pointer down/move/up command and wait for the remote player's acknowledgement.

tools.name: disconnect_remote_device
tools.description: Close one authenticated player connection and reject its pending commands.

tools.name: clear_remote_device_data
tools.description: Discard one connected player's in-memory bounded logs, metrics, and latest screenshot without disconnecting it.

tools.name: create_vfx_trail
tools.description: Create a persistent Babylon ribbon/tube trail following a mesh or transform node. When no generator is supplied, a reusable generator transform is created at the optional position.

tools.name: list_vfx_trails
tools.description: List persistent VFX trail meshes and their generator/geometry configuration.

tools.name: get_vfx_trail
tools.description: Read one VFX trail configuration.

tools.name: set_vfx_trail
tools.description: Update a persistent VFX trail's generator, geometry, material, or playback. Structural edits rebuild the trail while retaining its node id.

tools.name: delete_vfx_trail
tools.description: Delete one VFX trail mesh while retaining its generator node.

tools.name: get_particle_collision_planes
tools.description: Read persisted CPU or native GPU particle collision planes and exact execution-backend evidence.

tools.name: set_particle_collision_planes
tools.description: Replace up to eight CPU or native GPU particle collision planes. Collision positions/normals are in particle simulation space; restitution 0..1 controls bounce. GPU systems execute in the WebGL2 transform-feedback or WebGPU compute update shader without CPU particle readback.

tools.name: get_particle_collision_spheres
tools.description: Read persisted CPU or native GPU particle collision spheres and exact execution-backend evidence.

tools.name: set_particle_collision_spheres
tools.description: Replace up to eight CPU or native GPU particle collision spheres. GPU systems execute projection and restitution in the WebGL2 transform-feedback or WebGPU compute update shader without CPU particle readback.

tools.name: get_gpu_particle_interactions
tools.description: Read bounded GPU-particle collision settings plus exact backend, support, shader, compilation, dispatch, workload, and WebGL2 occupancy-field evidence. WebGPU uses direct storage-buffer pairs; WebGL2 uses a GPU-only 3D occupancy raster without CPU readback.

tools.name: set_gpu_particle_interactions
tools.description: Configure bounded native GPU particle collisions without CPU readback. WebGPU directly reads prior particle storage; WebGL2 rasterizes a GPU-only 3D occupancy field inside boundsMin/boundsMax at gridResolution 4..64 and samples a 3x3x3 voxel stencil. Radius is in centimeters; restitution and separationStrength are 0..1. At most 4096 particles and 64 accepted neighbors are processed.

tools.name: get_gpu_particle_collision_events
tools.description: Read collision-triggered secondary-particle output settings and exact native backend, shader, dispatch, reserved-capacity, WebGL2 event-texture, capture, latency, and no-readback evidence for one GPU particle system.

tools.name: set_gpu_particle_collision_events
tools.description: Configure GPU-only secondary particles spawned by native plane/sphere collisions in the same GPU system. Reserve 1..2048 source particles and 1..4 outputs per source (4096 total maximum), then set event lifetime, speed, size, velocity inheritance, spread, and RGBA. WebGPU reads the prior storage buffer; WebGL2 transports collision position/direction through two float event textures. No particle data is read back to the CPU. Configure a collision plane or sphere first.

tools.name: get_particle_attractors
tools.description: Read native CPU/GPU particle attractors configured as radial VFX force fields. Positive strength attracts; negative strength repels.

tools.name: set_particle_attractors
tools.description: Replace a particle system's native radial VFX force fields. Each field has world position `[x,y,z]` in centimeters and signed strength; positive attracts and negative repels.

tools.name: list_particle_assets
tools.description: List the `.npss` node particle system assets available in the project. Use `instantiate_particle_system` to bring one into the scene.

tools.name: list_vfx_graph_templates
tools.description: Search and category-filter the deterministic portable Babylon Node Particle template catalog. Use the exact catalogRevision returned here when creating a .npss VFX Graph asset.

tools.name: create_vfx_graph_from_template
tools.description: Compile-check and persist one real .npss Babylon Node Particle asset from a searched VFX template under its exact catalog revision. The asset remains editable in the normal Node Particle editor.

tools.name: list_particle_systems
tools.description: List standard and GPU particle systems in the active scene, including their emitter and core settings.

tools.name: list_node_particle_systems
tools.description: List Node Particle System Set meshes and their graph/system counts in the active scene.

tools.name: get_node_particle_batch_release
tools.description: Read one Node Particle mesh's release-on-disable policy, exact state revision, live batch allocation, release/rebuild counts, and explicit Unity compatibility boundary.

tools.name: set_node_particle_batch_release
tools.description: Under the exact inspected lifecycle revision, opt one Node Particle mesh into or out of releasing its live particle-system batch when disabled. Re-enabling rebuilds from its retained graph; a failed change rolls the policy back.

tools.name: instantiate_particle_system
tools.description: Instantiate a `.npss` particle system asset into the scene, or create a default one when no `path` is given. Optionally attach it to an emitter node and position it (centimeters). Good for effects like fire, smoke, sparks or rain.

tools.name: delete_particle_system
tools.description: Dispose one native CPU or GPU particle system and remove its persisted events, collision volumes, GPU collision-event output, pairwise GPU interactions, vector fields, texture fields, and incoming proximity-event references. The emitter node is retained and can be deleted separately.

tools.name: get_node_particle_system_graph
tools.description: Read an existing Node Particle System Set's complete serialized graph.

tools.name: replace_node_particle_system_graph
tools.description: Replace and rebuild a Node Particle System Set from a serialized graph. Read the current graph first, then modify it deliberately.

tools.name: get_node_particle_code_graph
tools.description: Read a bounded paginated Node Particle graph for the Inspector canvas: exact block ids, classes, typed ports, embedded values, reachability to SystemBlocks, edges, and a canonical fingerprint. Prefer numeric block ids when names are duplicated.

tools.name: connect_node_particle_blocks
tools.description: Connect exact typed Node Particle ports with compatibility, hierarchy/cycle, and occupied-input validation. The complete candidate graph is rebuilt first; the live particle set changes only after a successful build.

tools.name: disconnect_node_particle_blocks
tools.description: Disconnect one exact Node Particle target input. Optional source block/output fields are stale guards. The live particle set changes only after the resulting complete graph rebuilds successfully.

tools.name: set_node_particle_block_input
tools.description: Set one disconnected embedded Node Particle input value by exact block id/name and port. Connected inputs reject until disconnected. The graph is atomically rebuilt before publication.

tools.name: validate_node_particle_code_graph
tools.description: Build an isolated clone of a Node Particle graph and report exact compiler/runtime errors, disconnected required inputs, unreachable blocks, block/edge/SystemBlock counts, built system count, and fingerprint without changing the active effect.

tools.name: set_particle_system_properties
tools.description: Set serializable standard/GPU particle properties by dotted path, for example `emitRate`, `minSize`, `maxSize`, `minLifeTime`, `maxLifeTime`, `direction1`, `direction2`, `blendMode`, or `particleTexture` settings.

tools.name: set_particle_system_playing
tools.description: Start or stop a standard or GPU particle system in the editor preview. When starting, optional bounded simulationSteps waits for render readiness and runs 1–120 update-only steps for deterministic external verification; set manualEmitCount first when particles must be emitted immediately.

tools.name: validate_particle_system
tools.description: Validate a CPU or GPU particle effect before export. Reports invalid emitter/capacity/lifetime/size settings, missing texture or zero-rate warnings, and an estimated peak particle budget. It does not modify the effect.

tools.name: list_vfx_budget_profiles
tools.description: List persisted scene-wide CPU/GPU particle quality profiles.

tools.name: create_vfx_budget_profile
tools.description: Create a reusable quality profile that scales particle capacity and emission, optionally clamping capacity.

tools.name: set_vfx_budget_profile
tools.description: Update a persisted particle quality profile.

tools.name: apply_vfx_budget_profile
tools.description: Apply capacity/emission scaling to all native CPU/GPU particle systems in the open scene.

tools.name: delete_vfx_budget_profile
tools.description: Delete a profile without reverting already applied particle settings.

tools.name: get_particle_vector_fields
tools.description: Read persisted bounded directional force fields for a CPU particle system.

tools.name: set_particle_vector_fields
tools.description: Replace up to eight bounded directional vector fields on a CPU particle system. Fields apply force per second inside their min/max 3D bounds.

tools.name: get_particle_texture_vector_fields
tools.description: Read persistent image-sampled 2D or depth-stacked 3D XYZ vector fields for a CPU or GPU particle system. GPU responses include exact native WebGPU/WebGL2 3D-atlas, compile, dispatch, sampling-bound, and no-readback evidence.

tools.name: create_particle_texture_vector_field
tools.description: Import one image (2D) or ordered image slices (3D) as a capped 1–64 voxel CPU/GPU particle vector field. RGB maps to signed XYZ direction (-1 to +1); the portable grid is embedded in scene metadata. GPU systems atomically upload enabled fields into one bounded native RGBA8 3D atlas sampled by WebGPU compute or WebGL2 transform feedback without readback.

tools.name: set_particle_texture_vector_fields
tools.description: Atomically replace all persistent 2D or depth-stacked 3D image-sampled CPU/GPU particle vector-field grids. GPU resources are built before publication and rolled back on failure. Prefer create_particle_texture_vector_field for normal image importing.

tools.name: get_particle_events
tools.description: Read persistent named burst events for one standard or GPU particle system.

tools.name: get_particle_proximity_events
tools.description: Read bounded CPU particle proximity rules that emit bursts into a target particle system.

tools.name: set_particle_proximity_events
tools.description: Configure bounded CPU particle-to-particle proximity rules. Matching particles emit a count into the target system; GPU particle systems are not supported.

tools.name: set_particle_events
tools.description: Replace up to 32 named gameplay burst events on a standard or GPU particle system. Trigger them from game code using the exported triggerParticleEvent helper or in the open editor with trigger_particle_event.

tools.name: trigger_particle_event
tools.description: Fire a configured named VFX burst event on one particle system or every matching system. Works with CPU and GPU particles; this is an external/gameplay event, not GPU particle-to-particle event chaining.

tools.name: list_audio_mixer_snapshots
tools.description: List saved mixer-bus gain and mute snapshots.

tools.name: create_audio_mixer_snapshot
tools.description: Capture current audio-bus gains and mute states as a named snapshot.

tools.name: apply_audio_mixer_snapshot
tools.description: Apply a saved snapshot immediately or blend its gain and pitch values over bounded time; mute and solo states switch when the blend completes.

tools.name: delete_audio_mixer_snapshot
tools.description: Delete a saved mixer snapshot.

tools.name: list_audio_buses
tools.description: List persisted hierarchical mixer buses.

tools.name: get_audio_mixer_runtime
tools.description: Read resolved Master paths, hierarchy depth, inherited gain and pitch, mute/solo audibility, native Babylon AudioV2 bus connectivity, active snapshot-blend progress, and validation warnings.

tools.name: list_audio_runtime_diagnostics
tools.description: Inspect every SoundNode's loaded/playing state, spatial mode, base/effective volume, mixer-bus influence, and stale mixer assignments. This reads current preview/runtime state without changing playback.

tools.name: get_audio_mixer_profile
tools.description: Read opt-in newest-first Audio Mixer timeline samples and cumulative summaries for synchronous mixer CPU time, total/playing/spatial/streaming voices, buses/effects/sends, active reverb zones, native connectivity, AudioContext sample rate/latency, per-bus estimated peak, and estimated clipping. The response explicitly distinguishes measurable JavaScript CPU and estimated source levels from native DSP-thread CPU and hardware clipping, which WebAudio does not expose.

tools.name: set_audio_mixer_profile
tools.description: Enable or disable transient Audio Mixer profiling and configure a 1–256-sample ring plus a 1–120-update sampling interval. Profiling measures the exact shared editor/export AudioMixer update path and adds bounded timer/counter overhead; retained history survives stop/start until cleared.

tools.name: clear_audio_mixer_profile
tools.description: Clear transient Audio Mixer samples, CPU/voice/signal summaries, overflow counters, and update counters while retaining enabled/capacity/interval settings.

tools.name: create_audio_bus
tools.description: Create a hierarchical mixer bus routed to Master or another bus, with inherited gain/pitch and exclusive SoundNode assignments.

tools.name: set_audio_bus
tools.description: Rename/reparent a mixer bus or change its gain, pitch, mute/solo state, and exclusive SoundNode assignments; cycles reject atomically.

tools.name: create_audio_send
tools.description: Create an audible post-fader return send or a control-only sidechain send between mixer buses. Sidechains drive bounded threshold/ratio/attack/release ducking without adding their signal to the target output.

tools.name: set_audio_send
tools.description: Update one return/sidechain send, including target, level, enabled state, kind, and complete sidechain ducking envelope.

tools.name: delete_audio_send
tools.description: Delete one return or sidechain send without deleting either bus.

tools.name: create_audio_effect
tools.description: Insert an ordered native WebAudio DSP effect on a mixer bus. Supports gain, low/high-pass, parametric EQ, compressor, distortion, echo, chorus, flanger, and stereo panning with wet/dry mix and bypass.

tools.name: set_audio_effect
tools.description: Rename, bypass, mix, retune, change type, or reorder one mixer DSP effect atomically.

tools.name: delete_audio_effect
tools.description: Delete one ordered DSP effect without deleting its mixer bus.

tools.name: list_audio_reverb_zones
tools.description: List persisted sphere/box reverb zones and current listener distance, blend weight, priority selection, target bus path, and native convolution connectivity.

tools.name: create_audio_reverb_zone
tools.description: Create a spatial sphere or box zone that blends one convolutionReverb mixer effect from the active camera/listener position in centimeters.

tools.name: set_audio_reverb_zone
tools.description: Retarget, move, resize, prioritize, enable, or change the shape and blend geometry of one reverb zone atomically.

tools.name: delete_audio_reverb_zone
tools.description: Delete one spatial reverb zone without deleting its target effect or bus.

tools.name: assign_sound_node_to_audio_bus
tools.description: Exclusively assign one SoundNode to a mixer bus, or pass null to clear its assignment and restore its base volume.

tools.name: delete_audio_bus
tools.description: Delete a mixer bus without deleting sounds.

tools.name: list_sound_assets
tools.description: List native sound clips and `.audio-generator.json` assets available in the project. Use this to find ambience/music files before calling `create_sound`. If nothing suitable exists, download more via the marketplace tools.

tools.name: list_audio_generators
tools.description: List indexed .audio-generator.json assets with exact dependency and build-readiness evidence.

tools.name: list_audio_generator_types
tools.description: List built-in and registered project generator node types, defaults, seek support, and portable graph limits.

tools.name: get_audio_generator
tools.description: Read one canonical graph, exact source/runtime fingerprints, revision, AudioClip leaves, and build readiness.

tools.name: create_audio_generator
tools.description: Create a canonical generated-audio graph asset; omit graph for an immediately audible oscillator graph. The parent folder must already exist.

tools.name: set_audio_generator
tools.description: Replace a complete graph under the exact source fingerprint from get_audio_generator; advances its persisted revision once.

tools.name: delete_audio_generator
tools.description: Delete one generated-audio graph and metadata under its exact inspected source fingerprint, with registry rollback on failure.

tools.name: validate_audio_generator
tools.description: Validate exactly one on-disk path (including dependency fingerprints) or one unsaved candidate graph without modifying project state.

tools.name: create_sound
tools.description: Create a `SoundNode` in the scene from a sound asset and load it (e.g. 'sounds of nature', 'people talking in the market place'). `spatial: true` (default) creates a 3D positional sound emitted FROM the node's transform — parent it under a node and/or set `position` (centimeters) to place the source (a fountain, a market stall, a campfire, a cluster of fireflies). `spatial: false` creates a global, non-positional 2D ambience/music bed that plays everywhere. Tune falloff with `maxDistance`/`distanceModel` ('linear'|'inverse'|'exponential') and stereo rendering with `panningModel` ('HRTF'|'equalpower'). After creation the node is selected and shown in the inspector.

tools.name: get_sound
tools.description: Read a SoundNode's asset, spatialization, attenuation, volume, and preview playback state.

tools.name: set_sound_playing
tools.description: Start or stop a SoundNode in the editor preview. startOffset is in seconds.

tools.name: set_sound_properties
tools.description: Update properties of an existing `SoundNode` (resolved by `nodeId`/`nodeName`). Only the provided fields are applied. Use this to adjust volume, switch between spatial/global, or retune falloff/panning after `create_sound`.

tools.name: list_video_players
tools.description: List every normalized persistent Video Player plus live decode, clock, source, target, duration, readiness, and playback diagnostics.

tools.name: create_video_player
tools.description: Create and preview one persistent Unity-style Video Player from a project asset or HTTP(S) URL with material, named render-texture/API, camera-plane, or API-only output and complete clock/playback/audio/aspect/stereo/color settings.

tools.name: set_video_player
tools.description: Atomically update one exact-id/name Video Player and recreate its live preview target; failed source or target changes roll back to the prior player.

tools.name: control_video_player
tools.description: Play, pause, or seek one persistent Video Player in the running editor using its selected browser or deterministic scene clock.

tools.name: delete_video_player
tools.description: Delete one exact-id/name player and restore/dispose only its owned material, camera-layer, texture, listener, observer, and scene-map resources; the source asset remains.

tools.name: list_game_object_component_types
tools.description: List the closed first-class component registry, duplicate/dependency rules, and optional node-specific availability. Includes runtime Light2D and ShadowCaster2D provider components.

tools.name: inspect_game_object_components
tools.description: Inspect one node's exact ordered component stack, stable component ids, real adapter values, dependencies, duplicate rules, clipboard state, and SHA-256 mutation fingerprint.

tools.name: add_game_object_component
tools.description: Add one data, behavior, Physics Body 3D, Entity, Network Replication, Light2D, or ShadowCaster2D component under the exact inspected stack fingerprint. Duplicate and target-support rules are enforced atomically with editor Undo/Redo.

tools.name: set_game_object_component
tools.description: Update one stable component without replacing its identity. Type-specific fields are validated and applied to the actual transform, script attachment, PhysicsAggregate, or runtime data component with Undo/Redo.

tools.name: move_game_object_component
tools.description: Move one component to an exact 1-based authored order while preserving required dependency order. Transform remains fixed at order 0.

tools.name: remove_game_object_component
tools.description: Remove a stable component and its real adapter state under an exact lease. Required Transform removal is rejected; dependent rows require explicit cascade=true.

tools.name: reset_game_object_component
tools.description: Reset the selected transform, data, behavior script, or physics component to deterministic defaults while retaining its stable component identity where applicable.

tools.name: copy_game_object_component
tools.description: Copy an exact component snapshot into the shared editor/MCP clipboard and return its SHA-256 clipboard fingerprint for guarded paste.

tools.name: paste_game_object_component
tools.description: Paste guarded clipboard values onto a same-type target, or create a new duplicate-compatible component. Both target stack and clipboard fingerprints must match; Undo/Redo restores the complete state.

tools.name: inspect_ecs
tools.description: Read the complete versioned scene ECS configuration, exact revision/fingerprint lease, runtime report, and bounded typed-chunk world summary.

tools.name: replace_ecs_configuration
tools.description: Atomically replace the complete portable ECS schema, systems, settings, and sections under the exact authoring lease. This does not claim Unity Entities package or Burst-native binary identity.

tools.name: delete_ecs_configuration
tools.description: Delete the scene-owned ECS asset and dispose its runtime under the exact authoring lease after literal confirmation. The operation is rejected while Entity components remain.

tools.name: set_ecs_settings
tools.description: Patch bounded ECS enable, fixed-step, chunk, safety, tracing, and portable main-thread/Worker execution settings under the exact authoring lease.

tools.name: create_ecs_component_type
tools.description: Create one stable-id typed ECS component schema with bounded scalar, boolean, vector, or quaternion fields.

tools.name: set_ecs_component_type
tools.description: Patch one non-built-in ECS component type's display name, namespace, or assembly under the exact authoring lease; use field tools for schema changes.

tools.name: delete_ecs_component_type
tools.description: Delete one unreferenced non-built-in ECS component type after literal confirmation. System and authored-entity references are rejected.

tools.name: create_ecs_field
tools.description: Create one bounded typed field on an editable ECS component schema under the exact authoring lease.

tools.name: set_ecs_field
tools.description: Patch one exact ECS field definition; null minimum or maximum removes that bound. Cross-references and typed defaults are validated atomically.

tools.name: delete_ecs_field
tools.description: Delete one unreferenced ECS field after literal confirmation. System and authored-entity references are rejected.

tools.name: create_ecs_system
tools.description: Create one declarative fixed/update/late ECS system with a typed query, access declarations, dependencies, and portable compiled operations.

tools.name: set_ecs_system
tools.description: Atomically patch one ECS system while validating component access, operation fields, dependency phases, conflicts, and cycles.

tools.name: delete_ecs_system
tools.description: Delete one ECS system after literal confirmation when no remaining system depends on it.

tools.name: create_ecs_section
tools.description: Create one stable streaming section with authored auto-load behavior and deterministic priority.

tools.name: set_ecs_section
tools.description: Patch one ECS streaming section name, auto-load state, or priority under the exact authoring lease.

tools.name: delete_ecs_section
tools.description: Delete one unused non-main ECS streaming section after literal confirmation.

tools.name: validate_ecs
tools.description: Read-only validation of the complete ECS model, cross-references, dependency schedule, full bake report, and bounded world snapshot.

tools.name: bake_ecs
tools.description: Run a full or source-lease-guarded incremental bake into typed archetype chunks and return runtime, schedule, trace, section, and bounded world evidence.

tools.name: control_ecs_runtime
tools.description: Start, resume, pause, or stop the live ECS world under its exact generation and optional status lease.

tools.name: step_ecs_runtime
tools.description: Execute one bounded ECS frame with deterministic fixed/update/late ordering, deferred-command playback, and optional real Web Worker kernels.

tools.name: queue_ecs_runtime_command
tools.description: Queue one exact-generation field write, entity instantiate/destroy, or section load-state command for atomic deferred playback. Destroy requires literal confirmation.

tools.name: playback_ecs_runtime_commands
tools.description: Atomically validate and apply all queued exact-generation ECS structural commands, publishing a new generation only if every command succeeds.

tools.name: query_ecs_entities
tools.description: Read a bounded page of live entities by required, optional-any, excluded components, section, and loaded state, with optional typed field values.

tools.name: inspect_ecs_schedule
tools.description: Read the immutable compiled phase batches, dependency/conflict ordering, runtime backend evidence, and bounded execution traces.

tools.name: set_ecs_hierarchy_preferences
tools.description: Persist whether hidden Entities appear in the main Hierarchy and choose the authoring, runtime, or combined Entities debugger world under the exact authoring lease.

tools.name: query_ecs_hierarchy
tools.description: Read a bounded authoring, runtime, or combined Entity hierarchy page with name, parent path, hidden state, origin, archetype, section, and components. Runtime/combined reads require the exact live generation.

tools.name: query_ecs_systems_window
tools.description: Run the bounded Systems quick-search language and structured namespace, phase, enabled, read, write, and component filters under the exact authoring lease. Quick tokens use namespace:, phase:, enabled:, reads:, writes:, or component:.

tools.name: inspect_ecs_type_registry
tools.description: Read a bounded page of effective component registration status and assembly-wide policies. This is Zvibe's portable registry, not Unity TypeManager or C# attribute identity.

tools.name: set_ecs_type_registration_policy
tools.description: Create or replace one assembly-wide auto-registration policy under the exact authoring lease. When auto-registration is disabled, only explicit registeredTypeIds are usable by bakers and compiled systems.

tools.name: delete_ecs_type_registration_policy
tools.description: Delete one assembly-wide registration policy under the exact authoring lease after literal confirmation, restoring automatic registration for that assembly.

tools.name: get_editor_extension_sdk
tools.description: Get the versioned Zvibe Editor extension manifest, lifecycle, capability, contribution, trust, and bounded-runtime contract without inspecting or executing installed package code.

tools.name: list_editor_extensions
tools.description: Inspect direct project dependencies for strict zvibeEditor manifests and return exact package/content fingerprints, shared enablement, machine-local trust, runtime state, issues, and pagination without executing extension code.

tools.name: plan_editor_extension_change
tools.description: Create a single-use 15-minute exact-state plan to enable, disable, trust, revoke trust for, or remove shared configuration for one installed editor extension. Trust requires the exact currently requested capability set.

tools.name: apply_editor_extension_plan
tools.description: Apply one exact, non-expired, single-use extension plan. Shared enablement changes are persisted to the project; trust changes stay machine-local. Current package/config/trust fingerprints must still match.

tools.name: reload_editor_extension
tools.description: Dispose, re-inspect, trust-check, and reactivate one active editor extension only when its exact runtime fingerprint still matches.

tools.name: open_editor_extension_window
tools.description: Open a manifest-declared dockable window owned by one active extension under its exact runtime fingerprint.

tools.name: invoke_editor_extension_menu
tools.description: Invoke a manifest-declared menu command owned by one active extension under its exact runtime fingerprint; extension failures and timeouts are returned.

tools.name: list_build_profile_footer_actions
tools.description: List paginated active extension actions that match one selected Build Profile target and active state, including exact profile revision and extension fingerprints, without executing extension code.

tools.name: invoke_build_profile_footer_action
tools.description: Invoke one active manifest-declared Build Profile footer action after exact Build Profile revision, package content fingerprint, declaration, target filter, and active-profile eligibility checks.

tools.name: run_editor_extension_tests
tools.description: Run up to 100 selected manifest-declared editor-only tests from one active extension, sequentially, with a 30-second maximum per-test timeout and exact runtime fingerprint guard.

tools.name: get_project_collaboration_capabilities
tools.description: Inspect the exact Unity-comparable collaboration contract implemented by Zvibe Editor: roles, presence, revision-guarded scene edits, collaborative text and ordered data, semantic scene/prefab merge, asset locks, remote transports, and review workflows. Explicitly reports automatic-merge boundaries without changing the project or returning credentials.

tools.name: validate_project_collaboration_readiness
tools.description: Audit the open project's legacy-local, authenticated-local, semantic-conflict, review, gateway, relay, discovery, and federated-lock readiness. Uses the active MCP collaboration session when present, returns actionable findings, never changes project state, and never returns credentials.

tools.name: get_project_services_capabilities
tools.description: Read the exact provider-neutral service categories, resources, environment/deployment/emulator guarantees, secret boundary, and services that are deliberately not core adapters.

tools.name: get_project_services_configuration
tools.description: Read the exact revision, active environment, all provider-neutral service settings, resource catalogs, and deployment configuration without changing the scene.

tools.name: set_project_service_environment
tools.description: Create or update one development, staging, or production service environment at an exact revision. Deployment, when provided, replaces its fixed package script and credential environment-variable names; credential values are never accepted.

tools.name: set_active_project_service_environment
tools.description: Select the environment mirrored into exported runtime scene metadata. Requires the exact current revision and changes no remote provider state.

tools.name: delete_project_service_environment
tools.description: Delete one non-active, non-last service environment at an exact revision after explicit confirmation. Does not delete remote provider resources.

tools.name: set_project_service_category
tools.description: Replace one environment's auth, Cloud Save, analytics, IAP, ads, matchmaking, Leaderboards, Remote Config, Cloud Content Delivery, or Cloud Functions routing at an exact revision. Endpoints must be HTTPS or loopback HTTP at readiness/runtime; options accept only bounded non-secret scalars.

tools.name: set_project_service_resources
tools.description: Replace validated analytics schemas, IAP products, ads, matchmaking queues, leaderboards, Remote Config values, content buckets/releases/badges, and Cloud Function definitions for one environment at an exact revision.

tools.name: validate_project_services_readiness
tools.description: Audit runtime endpoints/provider boundaries, enabled categories, fixed deployment script presence, and credential environment-variable availability. Returns names/availability only, never credential values.

tools.name: plan_project_services_deployment
tools.description: Create a ten-minute no-write deployment plan from the exact service revision and package fingerprint. Defaults to dry-run, reports the shell-free command/readiness/resources, and never returns credential values.

tools.name: deploy_project_services
tools.description: Apply one exact unexpired valid plan after confirmation: atomically write the provider-neutral artifact, execute only the environment's fixed package script without a shell, and retain a bounded report. The project script may contact external providers.

tools.name: cancel_project_services_deployment
tools.description: Cancel the active bounded services deployment child process, optionally requiring its exact operation id; returns a no-op reason when none is running.

tools.name: list_project_services_deployment_reports
tools.description: List up to 20 retained bounded service deployment reports, newest first, without changing project or provider state.

tools.name: get_project_services_deployment_report
tools.description: Read one retained services deployment report by exact id, including bounded redacted stdout/stderr and artifact path.

tools.name: delete_project_services_deployment_report
tools.description: Delete one local retained deployment report after explicit confirmation; does not affect its artifact or remote provider resources.

tools.name: start_project_services_emulator
tools.description: Start one persistent HTTP development backend bound only to 127.0.0.1 for all ten portable service routes. Requires the exact configuration revision; port 0 selects a free local port. Writes only bounded local emulator state.

tools.name: stop_project_services_emulator
tools.description: Stop the active loopback emulator after draining accepted mutations. Persistent local test data remains available for restart.

tools.name: get_project_services_emulator_status
tools.description: Read loopback endpoint, environment, persistence path, uptime, and bounded local data counts without exposing sessions or credentials.

tools.name: get_project_services_emulator_events
tools.description: Read a bounded sequence page of sanitized local service actions, optionally filtered by category, action, or player id. Tokens and credentials are never recorded.

tools.name: reset_project_services_emulator
tools.description: Permanently clear all persistent local players, saves, events, purchases, ad impressions, tickets, and sessions for the running emulator after explicit confirmation.

tools.name: get_networking_capabilities
tools.description: Read the shipped client/server transport, replication, prediction, session, Multiplayer Play Mode, simulation, integration, and provider-boundary contract.

tools.name: get_networking_configuration
tools.description: Read the complete versioned scene networking configuration and exact authoring revision.

tools.name: set_networking_configuration
tools.description: Exact-revision patch the scene transport, replication, prediction/reconciliation, simulation, session, or trace configuration. Connection credentials are never accepted here.

tools.name: validate_networking_target
tools.description: Audit configuration, unique Network Replication ids, target security, authored readiness, and optional local runtime status without connecting.

tools.name: start_gameplay_session_host
tools.description: Start the bounded authenticated WebSocket gameplay host. Defaults to loopback and an automatic port; LAN exposure requires confirm=true and should use a trusted network or TLS terminator.

tools.name: stop_gameplay_session_host
tools.description: Disconnect all gameplay players, destroy every transient session, stop Multiplayer Play Mode, and close the listener.

tools.name: get_gameplay_session_host_status
tools.description: Read listener endpoint, bounded counts, errors, and transport security without exposing any credential.

tools.name: create_gameplay_session
tools.description: Create one transient private/public lobby under the exact scene revision and return its one-time host credential plus join code. Copy the host token immediately; it is never persisted.

tools.name: list_gameplay_sessions
tools.description: Page transient local lobbies. Public-only reads expose browseable join codes; editor-visible reads never expose host or reconnect tokens.

tools.name: get_gameplay_session
tools.description: Read one lobby, players, ownership/manifest counts, and relay metrics without host or reconnect tokens.

tools.name: set_gameplay_session
tools.description: Exact-revision update one transient lobby's name, capacity, visibility, host migration, or reconnect grace.

tools.name: delete_gameplay_session
tools.description: Delete one exact-revision transient lobby and disconnect its players. An active Multiplayer Play session must be stopped first.

tools.name: connect_networking_runtime
tools.description: Connect the exact compiled Play scene using memory-only host, join, or reconnect credentials. Credentials are never authored or returned in status/trace.

tools.name: disconnect_networking_runtime
tools.description: Close the compiled Play gameplay connection and cancel reconnect/simulation work without changing authored configuration.

tools.name: get_networking_runtime
tools.description: Read credential-free compiled Play connection state, authority, ownership, peers, replication metrics, simulation, and paged protocol trace.

tools.name: set_networking_ownership
tools.description: Claim or release one owner-authority Network Replication object through the connected gameplay host.

tools.name: submit_networking_input
tools.description: Apply and transmit one bounded owner input translation/rotation for client anticipation plus authoritative reconciliation and rollback/replay evidence.

tools.name: send_networking_rpc
tools.description: Send one bounded reliable or best-effort-simulated RPC to the server, all peers, or an object's owner.

tools.name: clear_networking_evidence
tools.description: Clear retained Play networking metrics and protocol trace without disconnecting.

tools.name: start_multiplayer_play_mode
tools.description: Start one exact compiled 1–4-player local test lease: the primary editor Play scene plus isolated compiled headless scenes/engines, optional unique owner assignments, and per-player adverse-network simulation.

tools.name: get_multiplayer_play_mode
tools.description: Read credential-free exact run revision, per-player roles, scenes, assignments, runtime metrics/simulation, and errors.

tools.name: control_multiplayer_play_mode
tools.description: Apply one exact-run pause/resume, deterministic virtual frame step, input, RPC, ownership, simulation, disconnect, or reconnect operation. Primary rendering remains editor-owned.

tools.name: stop_multiplayer_play_mode
tools.description: Disconnect every test player, dispose isolated scenes/engines, delete the transient session, and release only host/Play leases created by this run.

tools.name: get_mobile_capabilities
tools.description: Read the shipped on-screen touch, Android/iOS package/sign/device/log/store workflows, tool dependencies, security controls, and honest vendor boundaries.

tools.name: get_touch_controls_configuration
tools.description: Read the complete versioned on-screen button/stick configuration and exact scene revision.

tools.name: set_touch_controls_configuration
tools.description: Exact-revision patch runtime enabled, editor visibility, safe-area, or opacity settings.

tools.name: create_touch_control
tools.description: Create one bounded hand-editable on-screen button or fixed-center stick with a normalized viewport rect and Input Actions <touch>/ path.

tools.name: set_touch_control
tools.description: Exact-revision update one stable-id button/stick layout, binding, appearance, or value/deadzone field.

tools.name: delete_touch_control
tools.description: Delete one exact-revision on-screen control and clear its transient preview value.

tools.name: validate_touch_controls
tools.description: Audit viewport bounds, stable identity, uniqueness, appearance values, and Input Actions path bindings without changing the scene.

tools.name: simulate_touch_control
tools.description: Press, move, or release one authored control through the active Input Actions preview runtime without changing persisted authoring.

tools.name: get_touch_controls_runtime
tools.description: Read bounded active pointer and Input Actions values for the current editor viewport overlay.

tools.name: get_mobile_deployment_configuration
tools.description: Read exact-revision Android/iOS package, signing-environment-reference, output, and store settings; secret values are never returned.

tools.name: set_mobile_deployment_configuration
tools.description: Exact-revision patch Android/iOS native deployment settings. Credential/signing fields accept environment-variable names only, never secret values.

tools.name: validate_mobile_target
tools.description: Audit the exact deployment configuration, scaffold integrity, native project, host tools, environment references, package/device/store readiness, and vendor prerequisites without executing a workflow.

tools.name: plan_mobile_workflow
tools.description: Create a one-time ten-minute package/install/launch/log/store plan bound to exact deployment/scaffold revisions, artifact hash, device id, and required installed tools. Planning performs no native mutation.

tools.name: get_mobile_workflow_plan
tools.description: Read one unexpired exact-state Mobile plan and its artifact hash/warnings.

tools.name: execute_mobile_workflow_plan
tools.description: Consume and execute one exact Mobile plan through fixed no-shell vendor commands. May package/sign, mutate a connected device, capture logs, or submit to a configured store track; confirm=true is mandatory.

tools.name: get_mobile_job
tools.description: Read one retained Mobile job with redacted commands/output, lifecycle state, error, and hash-verified produced artifacts.

tools.name: list_mobile_jobs
tools.description: Page retained redacted Mobile package/device/log/store job evidence.

tools.name: cancel_mobile_job
tools.description: Confirm and terminate one active native vendor process while retaining its final redacted evidence.

tools.name: list_mobile_artifacts
tools.description: Page project-contained APK, AAB, and IPA artifacts with size, modification time, and SHA-256 evidence.

tools.name: list_mobile_devices
tools.description: Query installed adb or xcrun tooling for connected Android/iOS physical devices and simulators without changing them.

tools.name: get_adaptive_performance_capabilities
tools.description: Discover the Basic provider, Apple iOS/tvOS/visionOS bridge contract, six concrete Babylon quality scalers, thermal states, bottleneck signals, editor simulation, and explicit hardware-evidence boundaries. Use this before authoring a policy; it does not inspect or change scene state.

tools.name: get_adaptive_performance_configuration
tools.description: Read the complete normalized version-1 provider, platform, target cadence, indexer delays/hysteresis, all six scaler settings, exact revision, and matching live runtime evidence. Preserve configuration.revision before calling a write or transient control tool.

tools.name: set_adaptive_performance_configuration
tools.description: Atomically patch the Basic/Apple provider, target platform, bounded indexer timing, or one or more stable-id scalers under the exact current revision. The editor records Undo/Redo and restarts the shared preview/export runtime with exact baseline restoration. Apple on non-Apple targets and a missing native bridge remain visible warnings rather than fabricated support.

tools.name: get_adaptive_performance_runtime
tools.description: Read bounded active-provider/fallback source, frame/optional CPU/GPU timing windows, bottleneck, thermal warning, low-power state, quality index, every scaler level/applied action, last decision, warnings, errors, and the most recent 64 provider/actions events.

tools.name: simulate_adaptive_performance_state
tools.description: Under the exact authored revision, inject a clearly labeled non-hardware thermal state and/or 1–240 deterministic frame samples into the active editor runtime. Use thermal simulation to test Apple warning/scaler policy; use optional CPU/GPU times only with frameTimeMs to test bottleneck selection. This changes transient preview quality and evidence but never persisted authoring.

tools.name: reset_adaptive_performance_runtime
tools.description: Under the exact authored revision, restore every scaler-owned render/LOD/shadow/view/post-process/particle baseline and clear transient timing, thermal, warning, quality-index, and bounded action evidence without changing persisted configuration.

tools.name: get_mobile_system_capabilities
tools.description: Discover Android inset visibility/system-bar policy, native bridge contract, CSS evidence fallback, Apple Serious/Critical thermal FPS defaults, frame-gate ownership, simulation labels, and hardware boundaries.

tools.name: get_mobile_system_configuration
tools.description: Read the normalized exact-revision Android window-inset and iOS thermal frame-rate authoring plus current bounded runtime evidence.

tools.name: set_mobile_system_configuration
tools.description: Patch Android requested visible inset types/system-bar behavior or Apple Serious/Critical FPS under the exact authored revision, with editor undo/redo and runtime replacement.

tools.name: get_mobile_system_runtime
tools.description: Read bridge availability, applied inset policy, current pixel/visibility evidence, thermal source, applied FPS cap, rendered/skipped frames, warnings, errors, and the newest 64 events.

tools.name: simulate_mobile_system_state
tools.description: Under the exact revision, inject clearly labeled non-hardware Android inset and/or Apple thermal evidence for editor verification. This never claims device evidence or changes authoring.

tools.name: reset_mobile_system_runtime
tools.description: Clear transient inset, thermal, frame-pacing, warning/error, and event evidence under the exact authored revision without changing configuration.

tools.name: get_grpc_transport_capabilities
tools.description: Discover the portable fetch-based gRPC-Web binary/text and Connect protocols, unary/server-streaming support, framing, trailers, deadlines, message limits, transient metadata, and browser/native HTTP/2 boundaries.

tools.name: get_grpc_transport_configuration
tools.description: Read the exact-revision endpoint/protocol/deadline/message limits/non-secret default metadata plus bounded call evidence.

tools.name: set_grpc_transport_configuration
tools.description: Patch portable gRPC-Web/Connect transport authoring under the exact revision. Remote endpoints require HTTPS, HTTP is loopback-only, and secret-bearing default metadata is rejected.

tools.name: invoke_grpc_unary
tools.description: Send one protobuf message through the authored endpoint and return bounded base64 response, HTTP/gRPC status, exposed headers/trailers, sizes, and duration. Per-call metadata is transient.

tools.name: invoke_grpc_server_stream
tools.description: Send one protobuf request and collect at most 256 bounded gRPC-Web/Connect server-stream messages with trailers and status. Browser CORS and fetch streaming constraints still apply.

tools.name: get_grpc_transport_runtime
tools.description: Read bounded non-secret evidence for the newest 32 calls, including protocol, method, sizes, counts, status, duration, and redacted error text.

tools.name: get_console_server_capabilities
tools.description: Read the production NullEngine/WebSocket/container/Kubernetes/fleet surface, licensed-provider contract, security controls, and honest external boundaries.

tools.name: get_console_server_configuration
tools.description: Read exact-revision headless, container, deployment, and observability settings. Only environment-variable names are persisted.

tools.name: set_console_server_configuration
tools.description: Exact-revision patch production server, container, provider, fleet, or observability settings with Undo/Redo.

tools.name: list_console_providers
tools.description: List strict project-contained licensed console provider manifests plus isolated bounded validation errors.

tools.name: get_console_provider
tools.description: Read one exact provider manifest, declared platforms, environment references, fixed commands, and content fingerprint.

tools.name: validate_console_server_target
tools.description: Audit exact authoring, selected headless Build Profile/scene, scaffold and deployment hashes, host commands, provider manifest, and environment references without executing anything.

tools.name: generate_server_deployment_artifacts
tools.description: Generate hash-owned Kubernetes, environment-example, and deployment documentation files under .zvibe/server against exact configuration/scaffold revisions.

tools.name: get_server_deployment_artifacts
tools.description: Read the deployment artifact revision, exact source revisions, generated files, and SHA-256 integrity evidence.

tools.name: remove_server_deployment_artifacts
tools.description: Confirmed exact-revision removal of only hash-owned files under .zvibe/server; modified files require forceModified=true.

tools.name: plan_console_server_workflow
tools.description: Create a single-use ten-minute plan bound to exact configuration, headless scaffold, deployment artifact, and console-provider fingerprints. Planning performs no external mutation.

tools.name: get_console_server_workflow_plan
tools.description: Read one unconsumed exact-state plan and expiration evidence.

tools.name: execute_console_server_workflow_plan
tools.description: Consume and execute one exact plan through fixed no-shell Node/container/Kubernetes/licensed-provider commands. confirm=true is mandatory.

tools.name: get_console_server_job
tools.description: Read one retained job with redacted bounded output, fixed commands, and lifecycle evidence.

tools.name: list_console_server_jobs
tools.description: Page retained redacted build, validation, deployment, fleet, log, profile, and certification job evidence.

tools.name: cancel_console_server_job
tools.description: Confirm and terminate one active fixed-command process while retaining final redacted evidence.

tools.name: list_server_instances
tools.description: Page editor-launched local instances and externally evidenced fleet operations without claiming provider-side discovery.

tools.name: get_server_instance
tools.description: Read one retained server-instance lifecycle, endpoint, job, and bounded output record.

tools.name: stop_server_instance
tools.description: Confirm and stop only one local process launched by this editor. External fleets require an exact stop workflow plan.

tools.name: inspect_server_endpoint
tools.description: Read the configured HTTP health or metrics route with a five-second timeout and configured response-size bound.

tools.name: get_project_auditor_capabilities
tools.description: Read the portable asynchronous Project Auditor contract, analyzer categories, safe-fix scope, hard scan limits, and explicit Unity/Roslyn non-identity boundaries.

tools.name: get_project_auditor_state
tools.description: Read the exact global revision, current non-blocking audit job, and up to 20 bounded recent jobs without starting analysis.

tools.name: start_project_audit
tools.description: Start one cooperative background audit under the exact global revision. It checks compile-time Inspector serialization, resolved deprecated/future-obsolete TypeScript APIs, GPU-only particle textures with unnecessary CPU Readable output, and project/live sprite-atlas waste.

tools.name: get_project_audit
tools.description: Read one retained asynchronous audit's status, progress, settings, summary, result fingerprint, and exact job revision.

tools.name: list_project_audit_issues
tools.description: Read one stable filtered issue page under the exact job revision. Each issue includes deterministic identity, severity, source/node location, bounded evidence, recommendation, safe-fix availability, and resolution state.

tools.name: cancel_project_audit
tools.description: Request cooperative cancellation of the queued/running audit under the exact global revision; analysis never publishes partial fixes or changes project files.

tools.name: apply_project_auditor_fix
tools.description: After confirm=true, apply one supported issue fix under exact global, job, and issue leases. Version 1 only disables unnecessary CPU Readable texture-importer output for GPU-only Babylon particle properties; source texture bytes are never changed.

tools.name: get_platform_player_capabilities
tools.description: Read the bounded Electron/Linux LTO and IBUS/FCITX5 IME contract, macOS display-link/frame-pacing contract, limits, and explicit native toolchain/adapter boundaries.

tools.name: get_build_profile_platform_player_plan
tools.description: Inspect one Electron profile's normalized Linux variant/LTO/IME or macOS display-link plan, exact Build Profiles revision, applied environment/flags, warnings, and honest execution scope without building.

tools.name: prepare_platform_player_runtime
tools.description: Prepare bounded transient composition and frame-pacing evidence from one exact persisted Electron Build Profile. This changes no authored profile or build artifact.

tools.name: get_platform_player_runtime
tools.description: Read the prepared profile identity, exact transient revision, bounded IME composition history, measured frame-pacing statistics, backend, warnings, and limits.

tools.name: simulate_platform_player_ime
tools.description: Under the exact transient revision, inject 1–32 explicitly labelled editor-simulation composition start/update/end records. This validates lifecycle handling but is not Linux daemon/hardware evidence.

tools.name: sample_platform_player_frame_pacing
tools.description: Under the exact transient revision, capture 2–240 real requestAnimationFrame deltas in the current Electron renderer and publish min/max/mean/deviation/p95 plus the effective Chromium or native-adapter backend.

tools.name: reset_platform_player_runtime
tools.description: Clear only bounded transient IME and frame-pacing evidence under the exact runtime revision; persisted Build Profile settings are unchanged.

tools.name: get_asset_streaming_capabilities
tools.description: Read the disabled-by-default Windows Electron setting, priority order, project probe roots, byte/job bounds, portable asynchronous-file backend, and explicit lack of bundled Microsoft DirectStorage/GPU-decompression identity.

tools.name: get_build_profile_asset_streaming_plan
tools.description: Inspect one Electron Build Profile's normalized Windows opt-in and scheduler settings, exact Build Profiles revision, effective platform/backend, warnings, and native-adapter boundary without opening files or building.

tools.name: prepare_asset_streaming_runtime
tools.description: Prepare a transient priority scheduler from one exact persisted Electron Build Profile and current project root. This replaces prior transient streaming evidence but does not change the profile or project files.

tools.name: get_asset_streaming_runtime
tools.description: Read the prepared scheduler's exact runtime revision, queued/active requests, bounded event/totals diagnostics, and a paginated page of hash-only file-probe jobs. Use the latest revision before start, cancel, or reset.

tools.name: start_asset_streaming_file_probe
tools.description: Start one cancellable, priority-scheduled background read of a bounded range inside project assets/ or public/. Results retain only request state, byte count, and SHA-256—never file bytes or absolute paths. Poll get_asset_streaming_runtime for completion.

tools.name: cancel_asset_streaming_request
tools.description: Cancel exactly one currently queued or active file probe under the latest runtime revision. Completed evidence and all authored project files remain unchanged.

tools.name: reset_asset_streaming_runtime
tools.description: Clear terminal probe jobs and bounded scheduler evidence under the latest runtime revision. Reset is rejected while work is queued/active and never changes persisted Build Profile settings or files.

tools.name: list_animation_groups
tools.description: List the scene's animation groups: clips imported with a mesh asset (e.g. a glTF character's 'idle'/'walk' clips) AND groups authored with `create_animation`. Use this to discover what is already playable before previewing with `play_animation_group` or authoring a new one.

tools.name: play_animation_group
tools.description: Preview an animation group in the editor (e.g. play a character's 'idle' or 'walk' clip, or a freshly authored door-opening animation) so you can verify it with `get_screenshot`. This is for in-editor preview only — to make the animation play at runtime in the game, attach a BEHAVIOR script that calls `scene.getAnimationGroupByName(name)?.play()` when the relevant event occurs (e.g. the player approaches).

tools.name: stop_animation_group
tools.description: Stop a playing animation group. Omit `name` to stop ALL animation groups in the scene.

tools.name: create_animation
tools.description: AUTHOR a keyframe `AnimationGroup` that animates a node property over time (e.g. a door opening = animate `rotation.y` from 0 to ~1.57 radians, a platform bobbing up and down = animate `position.y`, a light pulsing = animate `intensity` or `diffuse`). `targetProperty` is a dotted path on the resolved node (e.g. `"rotation.y"`, `"position"`, `"scaling"`, `"material.albedoColor"`). `keys` are `{ frame, value }` pairs; `value` is a number for scalar properties or `[x,y,z]` for Vector3/Color3 properties. `loopMode`: 'cycle' (restart from the first key, default), 'constant' (stop and hold the last key), or 'relative' (offset and continue from the end value). This creates REAL, hand-editable editor content (visible and tweakable in the Animation Groups inspector) — it does NOT make anything play yet. #1 RULE: do NOT animate the property directly from a script's `onUpdate` (e.g. incrementing `rotation.y` every frame) — author the motion HERE as a real AnimationGroup, then have a BEHAVIOR script call `scene.getAnimationGroupByName(name)?.play()` when something happens (the player approaches, a button is pressed, etc.). Preview the result with `play_animation_group` and `get_screenshot`.

tools.name: list_animation_events
tools.description: List persistent frame-event callbacks for one AnimationGroup or every group, including exact per-group revisions and bounded runtime dispatch evidence for editor and exported-game parity.

tools.name: set_animation_events
tools.description: Under the exact revision from list_animation_events, replace one AnimationGroup's persistent callbacks. Supports log, node enablement, group playback, and attached script-method dispatch with bounded JSON arguments plus error/warning/ignore missing-method reporting. Events execute identically in editor preview and exported games.

tools.name: get_animation_group
tools.description: Get an AnimationGroup's serialized graph plus every track, target, curve/keyframe, and timing property.

tools.name: get_animation_window
tools.description: Inspect one AnimationGroup through the standalone Unity-style Animation Window model. Returns an exact SHA-256 edit lease, clip duration, every target/property track, component labels, normalized scalar component values/tangents, interpolation, unique frames, and frame events for multi-track Dope Sheet or Curve editing.

tools.name: get_animation_runtime_debug
tools.description: Inspect one standalone AnimationGroup's live started/playing/paused state, current and normalized frame, loop count, speed, weight, animatables, paginated target current/evaluated values and divergence, recent Animation Events, runtime-only frame breakpoints, and bounded play/pause/loop/end/step trace. Returns an exact SHA-256 debugger lease for set_animation_runtime_debug or step_animation_runtime_debug.

tools.name: set_animation_runtime_debug
tools.description: Under the exact debugger fingerprint, atomically pause/resume a started standalone AnimationGroup, replace up to 64 exact-frame runtime breakpoints, clear its bounded trace, or set live loop, non-zero speed, and weight controls. Debug state is runtime-only and does not alter the persisted clip graph.

tools.name: step_animation_runtime_debug
tools.description: Under the exact debugger fingerprint, deterministically sample one started and paused standalone AnimationGroup by 1–120 exact frame steps totaling at most 10,000 frames. Stepping honors loop/clamp behavior and halts at the first enabled frame breakpoint while remaining paused. It does not advance the scene clock or replay Animation Event callbacks.

tools.name: edit_animation_window_keys
tools.description: Atomically edit 1–2048 exact keys across multiple AnimationGroup tracks using the fingerprint from get_animation_window. Move in time and optionally value, scale around a pivot, duplicate, delete, set linear/step interpolation, or offset selected scalar/vector/color/quaternion components. Rejects stale leases, missing keys, invalid components, empty tracks, and frame collisions.

tools.name: record_animation_window_properties
tools.description: Atomically record 1–128 current Inspector property values at one frame using the exact fingerprint from get_animation_window. Creates missing number/Vector2/Vector3/Quaternion/Color3/Color4 tracks or adds/replaces keys on existing target/property tracks. Returns per-property target, value, track-creation/key-replacement evidence and a fresh fingerprint; rejects stale leases, unsafe/unresolved paths, unsupported/non-finite values, duplicate entries, and type mismatches without partial mutation.

tools.name: set_animation_window_tangent_modes
tools.description: Atomically apply auto, clampedAuto, linear, linked freeSmooth, independent broken, or weighted tangent modes to 1–2048 exact Animation Window key selections under its SHA-256 fingerprint. Whole-key selections affect every component; component selections affect one curve. Weighted mode executes through Babylon's fixed-time Hermite model by scaling authored slopes by 3×weight, making weight 1/3 neutral; the response discloses authored slopes, weights, effective runtime tangents, lock state, persisted mode metadata, and a fresh window. Rejects stale leases, overlaps, invalid mode-specific fields, non-finite values, and out-of-range weights without partial mutation.

tools.name: open_animation_window
tools.description: Open the editor's shared standalone Animation Window on one existing AnimationGroup, selecting its multi-track Dope Sheet/Curve workflow without changing animation data.

tools.name: set_animation_keys
tools.description: Replace all keys in one AnimationGroup track. Use get_animation_group to discover target tracks and preserve the target property/type.

tools.name: set_animation_curve_keys
tools.description: Replace all keys in one scalar AnimationGroup track for the interactive curve-editor workflow. This rejects vector/color/quaternion tracks, duplicate frames, and non-finite values; use set_animation_keys for other track types.

tools.name: set_animation_curve_component_keys
tools.description: Replace one Vector2/Vector3/Color3/Quaternion component curve while preserving all other channels and requiring the track's existing frame set. Use component 0-3 and scalar values/tangents for multi-channel curve editing.

tools.name: set_animation_curve_tangents
tools.description: Set incoming and/or outgoing Hermite tangents at existing scalar or vector/color/quaternion animation keys without replacing their values. For multi-channel tracks, specify the component index.

tools.name: auto_smooth_animation_curve_tangents
tools.description: Recalculate centered tangents for every non-stepped key in one scalar, vector, color, or quaternion AnimationGroup track. Endpoint tangents use the available adjacent segment.

tools.name: sample_animation_curve
tools.description: Evaluate a scalar or vector component of an AnimationGroup track over a bounded frame range for curve visualization or analysis. Step keys hold; other keys interpolate linearly.

tools.name: export_animation_group
tools.description: Export one live AnimationGroup, including target identities, all typed curves/keys/tangents, loop state, events metadata, and importer evidence, to a contained project-relative Babylon AnimationGroup JSON file. Existing files require overwrite=true.

tools.name: import_animation_group
tools.description: Import a processed or exported Babylon AnimationGroup JSON from inside the project. Every target resolves before mutation through exact node, MorphTarget, or Sprite bindings. Converted Unity object-reference curves require a complete safe destination plus GUID/fileID/type value map; null, primitive, node, material, and contained texture values persist and execute in preview/export runtime. Duplicate, missing, ambiguous, unused, stale, unsafe, and unresolved bindings reject atomically. An existing group requires replaceExisting=true and is replaced only after parsing and runtime configuration succeed.

tools.name: delete_animation_group
tools.description: Remove and dispose an animation group from the scene by name (e.g. to remove a previously authored animation before re-authoring it).

tools.name: open_marketplace
tools.description: Open the marketplace browser tab inside the editor. ALWAYS go through the visible marketplace UI for searching/downloading assets — never call marketplace APIs in the background — so the user can watch the assets and download progress in the editor.

tools.name: search_marketplace
tools.description: Search a marketplace, driven through the editor's visible marketplace browser (not background APIs). Returns results with ids you can pass to `download_marketplace_asset`. Keep assets web-friendly: textures up to 4K (the editor can compress to KTX2) and meshes with a reasonable polygon count.

tools.name: download_marketplace_asset
tools.description: Trigger a VISIBLE download of a marketplace asset into the project via the editor's marketplace browser, so the user sees the progress. Returns the downloaded asset path. Choose a reasonable resolution (max 4K for textures) to keep the scene performant. After downloading, use `list_assets`/`get_asset_preview` then place it with `instantiate_mesh_asset` or `assign_texture_to_material`.

tools.name: get_inspector_collection_capabilities
tools.description: List typed visibleAsArray/visibleAsList authoring, bounded row operations, and DataTypeStyleMapper-compatible built-in or extension-registered styles.

tools.name: list_script_templates
tools.description: List built-in TypeScript behavior-script templates for use with create_script.

tools.name: list_scripts
tools.description: List the TypeScript scripts under the project's `src/` folder. Scripts implement behaviors (`onStart`/`onUpdate`/`onStop`) and are attached to nodes.

tools.name: list_custom_script_templates
tools.description: List bounded reusable project-local script-template metadata and exact fingerprints without returning source content.

tools.name: get_custom_script_template
tools.description: Inspect exact source content and SHA-256 fingerprint for one project-local custom script template before replacing or deleting it.

tools.name: set_custom_script_template
tools.description: Create a reusable project-local TypeScript template, or atomically replace an inspected template using its exact expectedFingerprint.

tools.name: delete_custom_script_template
tools.description: Permanently delete one exact inspected custom script template. Requires its fingerprint and explicit confirmation.

tools.name: get_script_debugger_capabilities
tools.description: Inspect Debug Play breakpoint, safe-boundary pause, variable snapshot, coverage, export, and explicit limitation contracts without starting Play.

tools.name: prepare_script_debugger
tools.description: Enable and compile source-instrumented Debug Play, or disable probes and rebuild a running Play scene. This affects only editor Play, never exported builds.

tools.name: get_script_debugger
tools.description: Read the exact instrumented manifest lease, resolved breakpoints, current hit, bounded trace, safe field snapshot, and attached-script pause state.

tools.name: set_script_breakpoints
tools.description: Atomically replace up to 64 runtime breakpoints under an exact source-manifest and debugger-configuration lease; requested lines resolve to the next executable point in the same file.

tools.name: control_script_debugger
tools.description: Pause/resume attached-script lifecycle delivery, advance one bounded fixed step while paused, or clear retained breakpoint-hit evidence under exact expected state.

tools.name: get_script_source_coverage
tools.description: Read source-level file/line/statement/function/branch coverage plus bounded exact source-point hits from instrumented Debug Play.

tools.name: set_script_source_coverage
tools.description: Enable/disable source coverage and optionally clear accumulated hit counts under the exact debugger lease.

tools.name: export_script_source_coverage
tools.description: Atomically export an exact coverage revision as deterministic JSON or LCOV below .bjseditor/script-coverage/ without returning the potentially large report body.

tools.name: create_script
tools.description: Create a new TypeScript script using the editor's default skeleton. The path MUST live under `src/**` (scripts outside `src/` are not valid editor scripts). Scripts are for runtime BEHAVIOR ONLY (input, movement, game rules, AI, collision reactions, runtime spawning) — NOT for building the scene. Before writing a script, author the geometry, materials, lights and props with the editor tools (`create_primitive_mesh`, `instantiate_mesh_asset`, `create_material`, `create_instance`, `create_light`, `set_mesh_physics`) so they remain real, hand-editable assets. After creating, edit it with `write_script` and attach it to a node with `attach_script`.

tools.name: read_script
tools.description: Read the content of a TypeScript script file. Use before `write_script` to make incremental edits without losing existing code.

tools.name: write_script
tools.description: Overwrite a script's content. The file must be under `src/**`. Implement runtime behaviors with the editor's `IScript` interface (`onStart`/`onUpdate`/`onStop`) and export inspector-editable values where it helps reuse. Keep scripts to LOGIC, not scene construction: do not use `new Mesh`/`MeshBuilder`/`new StandardMaterial`/`new ...Light` to build geometry, materials or lighting in code — that content must be authored with the editor tools so the user can hand-edit it. Reference already-authored assets from the script (e.g. look them up by name, or expose exported values set via `set_script_exported_value`). Example: a door that opens when the player is near checks distance in `onUpdate` and plays an animation on the existing authored door mesh.

tools.name: rename_script
tools.description: Move or rename a TypeScript script inside src/.

tools.name: delete_script
tools.description: Permanently delete a script in src/. Requires confirmation.

tools.name: validate_script
tools.description: TypeScript-transpile a script and return syntax diagnostics.

tools.name: get_script_semantic_diagnostics
tools.description: Type-check one TypeScript behavior script and return semantic/syntax diagnostics with project-relative file, line, and column. Unlike validate_script, this catches type errors.

tools.name: get_project_script_semantic_diagnostics
tools.description: Type-check every TypeScript behavior script under src/ and return semantic diagnostics with source locations.

tools.name: get_script_runtime_diagnostics
tools.description: Read live lifecycle, deterministic-manual-step call counts, exact last manual delta, and latest error for attached behavior scripts on a node. Automatically resolves the corresponding runtime node in a ready Play scene; an empty scripts array means no behavior is active.

tools.name: get_script_exported_fields
tools.description: Discover visibleAs*-decorated script fields, including typed visibleAsArray/visibleAsList declarations, their source types/defaults, and bounded decorator text.

tools.name: attach_script
tools.description: Attach a script file to a node (the scene itself can also have scripts). This writes the node's script metadata exactly as the inspector's Scripts section does, so the attachment is visible to the user.

tools.name: list_attached_scripts
tools.description: List the scripts attached to a node along with their exported inspector values. Use this to discover which exported values you can tune with `set_script_exported_value`.

tools.name: set_script_exported_value
tools.description: Set an exported/inspector value of a script attached to a node. This lets you configure the same reusable script differently per object (e.g. open distance, speed).

tools.name: set_attached_script_execution_order
tools.description: Set a deterministic execution order for one script attached to a node. Lower values initialize and update before higher values on that same object; equal values retain attachment order.

tools.name: list_scene_script_execution_orders
tools.description: List scene-wide execution orders by script path. These override individual attachment orders when this exported scene loads.

tools.name: set_scene_script_execution_order
